title: LCM Calculator
description: Find the Least Common Multiple of two numbers, calculated from their greatest common divisor.

formula.summary: The LCM of two numbers can be computed directly from their product and their GCD, avoiding the need to list out multiples.

faqs.question: What is the LCM used for?
faqs.answer: The LCM is most commonly used to find a common denominator when adding or subtracting fractions with different denominators, and in scheduling problems (like finding when two repeating events coincide).

faqs.question: Is there a faster way than listing multiples?
faqs.answer: Yes - once you know the GCD (via the Euclidean algorithm), the LCM formula LCM = (a×b)/GCD is much faster than listing out multiples of each number, especially for larger values.

seoContent.heading: LCM and GCD are two sides of the same coin
seoContent.body: For any two positive integers, their GCD and LCM are related by a simple identity: GCD(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b. This means once you've computed the GCD using the fast Euclidean algorithm, finding the LCM is just one more division.

seoContent.heading: Where the LCM shows up in everyday math
seoContent.body: Beyond fractions, the LCM is useful anywhere repeating cycles need to be synchronized - like figuring out when two buses on different schedules will next depart at the same time, or aligning repeating patterns in music or manufacturing.
